faqs.question: What does the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of the Prothrombin G20210A mutation in the FII gene.

faqs.question: Why is the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test done?
faqs.answer: This test helps identify individuals at an increased risk of developing blood clots. It is mainly done to • Assess the risk of developing blood clots. • Assess the risk of venous thrombosis. • Inform appropriate preventive measures and treatment plans.

faqs.question: When is the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Doctors may recommend this test for • Individuals with a personal or family history of venous thrombosis, • Individuals who are taking oral contraceptives and have experienced a venous thrombotic event. • Pregnant women.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results, i.e., reports indicating that the mutation is present, mean that there is an increased risk of developing blood clots. Abnormal results do not necessarily mean you have a clot or a serious condition, but it's important to discuss them with your doctor for further evaluation and appropriate management.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test?
faqs.answer: For this test: • A sample of 3-5 ml of your EDTA whole blood will be required. • The collection procedure is quick and simple, involving a blood draw.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test?
faqs.answer: To prepare for this test: • No fasting or special diet is needed. • Make sure to inform your doctor about any medications you are taking, as certain drugs can interfere with the test results. • Follow any additional instructions given by your doctor regarding medications or other preparations. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test include: • Complete Blood Count (CBC): This test evaluates different components of your blood, including red and white blood cells, to assess overall blood health. • Coagulation Panel: This panel includes various tests to evaluate clotting factors and assess the overall functioning of the coagulation system.

faqs.question: What is the Prothrombin G20210A (Factor II) Mutation test also known as?
faqs.answer: FII G20210A Mutation test, Prothrombin Gene Mutation test

faqs.question: What is venous thrombosis?
faqs.answer: Venous thrombosis refers to the formation of blood clots in the veins, usually in the legs or pelvis. It can cause pain, swelling, and potentially serious complications if the clot dislodges and travels to other parts of the body.
